shots.text: Frostmere is a frozen sea in the north. The Tidefolk build their towns on the ice. Its Warden, Thalassa, sleeps in the water under it.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: A vast frozen sea in the dark, stilt towns, pearl-white harbours lit by torches.

shots.text: We fought there in the dark. Thalassa had gone mad, and the sea under the ice rose against the Tidefolk. It broke the ice from underneath, and the drowned climbed out of the holes: fishermen still casting their nets, priests still praying. They were led by the Tidefolk's own high priestess, the Saltmother.
shots.speaker: narrator
shots.art_note: The ice of Frostmere cracking open from below. Drowned fishermen with nets and drowned priests climbing out of the black holes, crabs crusted with ice behind them. Inside a tall column of black seawater, a woman walks: the Saltmother.

shots.text:
Fennick always said water slows. Not this water. In the margin of his notes he wrote one word: fire.

So we burn it.
shots.speaker: tamsin
shots.art_note: Tamsin on the ice at Netmend with Fennick's spectacles hanging round her neck, his notebook open.
